summary.text: At a harvest feast on the Achelous, the river-god in his own voice told how Heracles wrestled him for Deianira, how Nessus died by the Evenus with a poisoned arrow, and how the centaur's blood on a shirt consumed the hero on Mount Oeta — Ovid's ninth book pausing its march for Achelous' inset tale of love, jealousy, and mistaken charm.

chapters.title: Achelous' feast
chapters.text: Theseus and others had gathered where the Achelous ran high after rain; the river-god, horn restored with fruits by the Naiads, spread a banquet and began to speak. He told how Heracles came to Calydon and wrestled him for Deianira — how the hero broke his horn and won the bride. The full wedding and parentage dispute live on the Heracles shelf; here the river keeps only the contest in his own voice.

chapters.title: Nessus
chapters.text: Achelous continued: Heracles crossed the Evenus with Deianira, and the centaur Nessus ferried her for hire. Nessus tried to ravish her; the hero shot him with an arrow dipped in the Hydra's gall. Dying, the centaur gave Deianira his blood, swearing it would bind her husband's love if ever it waned — the lie that would undo them both.

chapters.title: The poisoned robe
chapters.text: When Heracles sacked Oechalia and brought Iole home, Deianira smeared the supposed charm on a robe and sent it by Lichas. The garment clung to his flesh; he tore at his own body on Mount Oeta and ordered a pyre built. Deianira, learning what she had done, hanged herself — and a cloud bore the hero to Olympus to wed Hebe.
